question:
Batch 69 = RULING 73 (orchestrator 2026-11-13 '18:00'), verbatim: "THE CUT FOLLOWS THE LOCK'S WORDS. (a) OUT: the out point is never before the decoded END of the lock's LAST word. A pause inside the locked text is not a cut point, however long: the sentence law looks for the tail pause only AFTER the last locked word. (The hook ended on 'or' at a 130 ms pause before 'reissued'.) (b) IN: the in point is never more than 400 ms before the first locked word's onset (and never less than the head-lead rule requires: 80 ms, or the declared pad). Dead air before the first word is trimmed to that lead; if the audio in that lead is not quiet by the head rule, hold with that reason. (clip_01 opened 3.47 s before 'I'.) (c) Both are checked at the pin-stage pre-check service too (ruling 68 / 72), so the builder learns before the seal that a span cannot be cut to these rules. Must-fail tests: both of 13949b7c's spans fail on the old code and pass on the fix; the three delivered pins' cuts are unchanged by it (0c68b589, 41f29b1f, 37c5b5f5: same in / out to the frame, or say which moved and why)."
Background (measured on the real run pinned_20261113_221758):
- the hook's pause_out (26.99-27.12) lies inside the decoded last word 'reissued.' (26.66-27.54). boundary() searches the quiet run between the two words' MIDPOINTS (a guard for Whisper's off edges), and the hesitation run's end (27.12) just crosses the midpoint (27.10).
- clip_01's decode has a 4.58 s hole before 'I' (14.44). The IN pause found is a 60 ms dip at 10.96, so the clip opens on 3.47 s of non-speech (the second recogniser hears no words; Whisper hallucinates 'thank you').
The change (pipeline/sentence_law.py, pipeline/lock_precheck.py):
- boundary(..., tail=False): with tail=True (only the edge after a lock's last word) the pause is searched from words[k]['end'] to the next word's midpoint. A run inside the last word cannot be chosen; a run crossing the decoded end still can.
- edge_plan calls boundary(sa, words, i1, tail=True), then _ruling73(bin_, bout, words, i0, i1), which narrows the legal ranges:
  - OUT cut_lo >= words[i1]['end'];
  - IN cut_lo >= words[i0]['start'] - IN_LEAD_MAX_S (0.400). The cut is moved to start - LEAD_TARGET_S (0.25) when it was before the bound. A file head keeps its quiet up to the bound.
  - Not cuttable when the range empties, with a reason naming (ruling 73 a / b).
  - The head-lead rule is untouched: ruling 28's hook_lead (80 ms) and the D1 pad still run, now inside the narrowed range.
- accepted_cut: a cut placed at the boundary point (DEC-10 d valley / short gaps) is clamped into [cut_lo, cut_hi], so no path cuts outside the ranges. G16 (_edge_row) reads the same ranges.
- sentence_law.lock_cut(src, words, lock, label): write_lock_cut_table's per-segment body moved verbatim (edge_plan, accepted_cut, hook_lead for the hook, the trimmed onset rule). write_lock_cut_table calls it, and so does the pre-check (c): after ruling 17 / 72 a span whose lock stands is cut with it, and an error holds with "ruling 73: the render cannot cut this span: ...". RULES becomes "ruling 17 + ruling 72 + ruling 73".
MEASURED (the cut table recomputed with the old and the new code on the runs' own files):
- 13949b7c: hook OUT 27.09 -> 27.78 (after 'reissued.'s end); clip_01 IN 10.97 -> 14.04; clip_01 OUT +20 ms; clip_02 unchanged.
- 0c68b589: unchanged (its clip_01 OUT recomputes one 10 ms hop off with the OLD code too).
- Every OUT of every delivered pin: unchanged.
- ONE span moves IN: 'Bitcoin ... ever.' (41f29b1f's hook 14.38 -> 14.57; 37c5b5f5's clip_02 14.38 -> 14.69). It opened 0.56 s before its first word. It is also the protected medley reference's hook, so that reference's reproduction reports the changed decision (an orchestrator ruling is pending; not merged).
Tests:
- test_ruling73.py: _ruling73 unit tests (a, b, file head); the must-fail on 13949b7c's real run (fails on the old sentence_law, passes on the fix); the delivered pins' cuts unchanged but the named span (fails on the old code because the named span did not move).
- test_lock_precheck.py: a span the render cannot cut holds before the seal; a passing span records the render's cut.
- 32 passed.
FIND: a path that can still cut outside the narrowed ranges (OUT before the decoded end, IN more than 400 ms early); a behaviour change for spans the rule does not touch (the refactor of write_lock_cut_table must be verbatim); the head-lead rule weakened; a pre-check verdict that differs from the render's cut table for the same span; a test that does not test what it claims. Only state what you can verify from the diff. Reply with the JSON verdict; keep the reasoning short; at most 4 findings.

consensus_findings.issue: accepted_cut's ruling-73 clamp only guards the point path; the fallback path returns cand['in'][0]/cand['out'][0] unclamped, so a candidate outside [cut_lo, cut_hi] still cuts outside the narrowed ranges
consensus_findings.evidence: cut_in = clamp(plan["in"], plan["in"]["point"]) if v["in"] and plan["in"].get("point") is not None else cand["in"][0]
consensus_findings.fix: Clamp the fallback too: cut_in = clamp(plan['in'], cand['in'][0]) (same for out), or assert the candidate lies in range.

rejected_findings.issue: _ruling73's IN narrowing can raise cut_hi above the original range, letting the IN cut sit after the first locked word's onset, outside the pause the plan validated; accepted_cut's clamp then trusts the widened hi
rejected_findings.evidence: hi = max(bin_["cut_hi"], bound) if bin_.get("file_head") else bin_["cut_hi"]   # a file head keeps its quiet
rejected_findings.fix: For non-file-head edges keep hi = min(bin_['cut_hi'], words[i0]['start']) (or the pause end) so the cut cannot land past the first word's onset; the file-head branch already shows the intended pattern.

rejected_findings.issue: The pre-check records the render's cut but never compares it against the plan's legality beyond cut['error']; a lock_cut that returns verified:False with a ruling-28/33 error (not via the cut.get('error') path... it does set error) still holds, but a successful cut whose values later drift from the render's own inputs (e.g. different SourceAudio decode) is recorded as the verdict with no equality check, so a pre-check verdict can differ from the render's cut table for the same span
rejected_findings.evidence: cut = sentence_law.lock_cut(a["path"], a["transcript"]["words"], lock, "hook" if s["role"] == "hook" else "clip")
rejected_findings.fix: Have the pin stage reuse the pre-check's recorded cut (or re-verify equality) so (c) guarantees the same verdict, rather than recomputing independently on possibly different transcripts/decodes.

missed_in_cycle2_unvoted.issue: _ruling73's IN narrowing sets cuttable = bool(bin_.get('cuttable')) and ok, but when the range empties (ok False) it keeps the OLD 'cut' value (target = bin_['cut'] if >= bound else start - LEAD_TARGET_S) which may lie outside the now-empty range; harmless because cuttable False blocks the cut, but the recorded 'cut' field is misleading
missed_in_cycle2_unvoted.evidence: bin_.update(cut_lo=bound, cut_hi=round(hi,3), cut=round(min(max(target, bound), hi),3), cuttable=... and ok, ...)
missed_in_cycle2_unvoted.fix: None needed; cosmetic only, or set cut=None when not cuttable.

missed_in_cycle2_unvoted.issue: TestTheDeliveredCuts.test_unchanged_but_the_named_span compares against MOVED hardcoded values (14.57/14.69) with a HOP=0.0101 tolerance, but it does not verify the moved IN actually satisfies ruling 73 (b) (cut_in >= start-0.400) nor that the moved value equals the ruling-73 bound (start-0.25); it only checks the cut moved to the expected number, so if _ruling73's target logic changed the test would still pass as long as the number matches
missed_in_cycle2_unvoted.evidence: want_in = MOVED.get((name, cid), o['cut_in']); self.assertLessEqual(abs(n['cut_in'] - want_in), HOP, ...)
missed_in_cycle2_unvoted.fix: Also assert n['cut_in'] >= words[i0]['start'] - SL.IN_LEAD_MAX_S for the moved spans, tying the test to the rule rather than the number.
